New consideration is unnecessary, but good faith and applicable formalities remain.
New consideration remains mandatory unless the parties both sign a waiver of that requirement.
questions.explanation: Article 2’s no-new-consideration rule is limited. It does not dispense with agreement, good faith, the statute of frauds or applicable signed-modification requirements.

questions.stem: Match the exchange problem to the best concept.
left: Promise made in gratitude for an already completed unbargained act
Promise leaving all performance entirely optional
Promise of extra pay for only an unchanged existing obligation
Genuine low-price sale intended as an exchange
choices: Past consideration problem
Illusory promise
Preexisting duty problem
Adequacy distinct from existence
questions.explanation: The distinctions concern timing, discretion, an existing duty and economic value. They require different analyses even though each involves a promise.

questions.stem: The doctrine asking whether a return promise or performance was sought and given in exchange is ___.
questions.explanation: Consideration identifies the exchange relationship. It is not merely another word for a benefit, a signature or reasonable reliance.

questions.stem: Which statement provides the clearest promise for an F7 analysis?
choices: “If approval fails, I will reimburse your nonrefundable room deposit up to 300 dollars.”
“I expect the board will approve, but I am not committing us to any expenses.”
“We might reimburse deposits after considering the proposals at next month’s meeting.”
“Your proposal is likely to succeed; the board has not made any commitment yet.”
questions.explanation: The reimbursement statement specifies a commitment, condition and cap. The others express interest or possibility without promising the requested action.

questions.stem: A tablet was purchased a week before the alleged reimbursement promise. Which F7 element is most directly missing for that purchase?
choices: Reasonableness, solely because reusable equipment can never support any reliance claim.
Foreseeability, solely because business equipment purchases are never foreseeable.
Causation: the later promise did not induce the earlier purchase.
The existence of a promise, solely because a promise made after an expense cannot be communicated.
questions.explanation: The chronology defeats the claimed causal link to that promise. Other facts may affect loss, but the later communication cannot have induced an already completed purchase.

questions.stem: A promise caps requested room-deposit protection at 300 dollars. The recipient instead books a 5,000-dollar package without consultation. What issue is especially important?
choices: Whether the later expenditure itself expands the earlier undertaking to cover the full package.
Whether the claimed expenditure reasonably relied on the limited promise.
Whether a loss above the cap conclusively proves that enforcing the entire proposed project is necessary.
Whether actual spending makes the scope of the communicated promise irrelevant to the claim.
questions.explanation: The scope of the communicated undertaking bears on reasonable reliance and relief. Spending after a promise does not automatically bring the entire expenditure within it.

questions.stem: A claimant proves a definite promise and some loss. What further analysis does F7 require?
choices: Whether the claimant subjectively hoped for payment, without examining the promise’s causal role.
Whether the expense followed the promise, treating chronology as sufficient proof of every remaining element.
Whether the expected contract profit exceeds the loss, treating that comparison as the sole injustice test.
Foreseeability, actual reasonable reliance, causation and the need to avoid injustice.
questions.explanation: F7 is an element-based alternative theory. Promise plus loss is not a complete substitute for the causal, reasonableness and injustice analysis.

questions.stem: An organizer requests a room reservation and specifically promises reimbursement if approval fails. Why might consideration and reliance both deserve discussion?
choices: The reservation must be consideration whenever it costs money, leaving no need to test exchange.
The reservation can support reliance only if no one ever requested it as a return performance.
The requested reservation may be an exchange, while induced reasonable loss may support an alternative reliance theory.
The same deposit may be recovered twice if the claimant establishes both theories separately.
questions.explanation: The theories focus on different relationships. An act may be sought as a return and also induced in reasonable reliance, but alternate theories do not justify duplicate recovery for the same loss.

questions.stem: A 240-dollar deposit is fully refunded after a project is canceled. Under F7, why does the refund matter?
choices: It establishes that the original action was never taken because of the promise.
It eliminates the promise’s definiteness, even if the reimbursement language remains unchanged.
It leaves the full deposit recoverable solely because the payment initially followed the promise.
It changes the remaining loss and the need for enforcement to avoid injustice.
questions.explanation: A refund does not rewrite the communication, but it affects what detriment remains and what relief justice may require. Distinguish formation of the promise from the consequences of reliance.

questions.stem: A person claims promissory estoppel to enforce an unwritten land bargain. What is the best course response?
choices: Check the governing writing rule and any applicable reliance exception separately.
The incurred reliance automatically supplies the missing memorandum for every land bargain.
The lack of writing automatically prevents any reliance-related exception from being considered.
The claimant’s sincere belief that the bargain was final conclusively defeats the writing defense.
questions.explanation: F7 does not supply a universal override of writing requirements. The interaction needs a specific exception or governing authority, rather than an absolute conclusion either way.

questions.stem: How does restitution differ from promissory estoppel in this introductory course?
choices: Restitution focuses on the claimant’s expenses alone, while estoppel requires enrichment of the defendant.
Restitution focuses on unjustly retained benefits; estoppel analyzes a promise and induced reliance.
Restitution requires a definite promise, while estoppel requires only a benefit conferred without one.
Both require the same promise and loss, so only the label changes the analysis.
questions.explanation: The theories have distinct focuses. Spending money does not necessarily confer a benefit on the defendant, and a received benefit does not itself establish a promise inducing reasonable reliance.

questions.stem: Match the evidence to the reliance question it most directly addresses.
left: A definite reimbursement message
A receipt dated after the message and testimony the booking depended on it
A reservation within the stated cap and requested purpose
No refund, credit or alternative recovery
choices: What was promised
Actual induced action
Reasonableness of reliance
Remaining detriment and injustice
questions.explanation: Each item supports a different part of F7. No single receipt proves every element; promise, causation, reasonable conduct and remaining loss need separate attention.

questions.stem: Under F7, the promise-based alternative to bargain enforcement analyzed in this lesson is called ___.
questions.explanation: Promissory estoppel requires the course’s promise, reliance, causation, reasonableness and injustice analysis; it is not automatic enforcement of every disappointing assurance.

questions.stem: Under D1, an ordinary minor’s contract is generally described how, subject to exceptions?
choices: Void from inception, leaving neither side any contractual rights under any circumstances.
Enforceable against the minor unless the adult first agrees to cancel it.
Voidable at the minor’s election.
Voidable solely at the adult’s election because the adult has full contractual capacity.
questions.explanation: The course distinguishes a protected party’s power to avoid from automatic nonexistence. Necessaries, ratification and restoration can require additional rules.

questions.stem: A party has a mental-health diagnosis. What is the appropriate capacity analysis?
choices: Treat the diagnosis itself as sufficient proof that every agreement is void.
Treat a signature as conclusive proof of capacity despite functional evidence to the contrary.
Evaluate only whether the price was fair, without examining the governing capacity test.
Examine the applicable functional test and transaction facts; diagnosis alone does not decide it.
questions.explanation: D1 does not treat a diagnostic label as a universal incapacity rule. Understanding, ability to act reasonably and the other party’s knowledge may matter under the governing test.

questions.stem: A seller knowingly lies about a failed inspection, but the buyer already knows the truth and buys only for spare parts. Which D2 element is missing on these facts?
choices: Inducement through justified reliance on the false assertion.
Falsity, because the buyer’s knowledge removes the difference between the statement and actual result.
A factual assertion, because an inspection result is only a statement of opinion.
Knowledge of falsity, because knowing the truth prevents the seller from intending deception.
questions.explanation: The lie remains false, but this buyer did not rely on it to enter the bargain. The avoidance theory requires that link; other possible wrongs need separate analysis.

questions.stem: A business urgently needs money and accepts a low offer. There is no improper threat. What is the best D2 conclusion?
choices: Urgency substitutes for an improper threat whenever the accepted price is unfavorable.
Financial pressure alone does not establish the course duress defense.
A low price alone proves that the other party caused the business’s financial pressure.
Accepting a needed payment establishes duress even when reasonable alternatives and threats are unexamined.
questions.explanation: Duress requires an improper threat inducing assent without a reasonable alternative. Need and a poor bargain do not themselves prove those elements, though other facts could change the analysis.

questions.stem: Both parties believe a pump exists in a sealed crate; it was destroyed before formation. The belief is basic and materially affects the exchange. What must still be addressed under D3?
choices: Whether the mistaken party later expressly asked the other party to cancel, which alone establishes the defense.
Whether the parties’ future resale predictions also proved inaccurate, which is required for every mistake claim.
Whether the buyer can show any price inequality, which alone substitutes for all risk-allocation analysis.
Whether the party seeking avoidance bears the risk of the mistake.
questions.explanation: Mutual mistake is not complete without risk allocation. Express terms or conscious acceptance of limited knowledge can assign the relevant uncertainty to the party seeking relief.

questions.stem: A functioning pump is sold, then market prices fall after formation. Why is this different from the destroyed-pump example?
choices: A later market change is not the same as a shared erroneous existing fact at formation.
The decline retroactively proves that both parties misunderstood the pump’s condition at formation.
Every failed shared price forecast is an existing-fact mistake merely because it influenced the bargain.
A later unfavorable market move automatically transfers the loss to the seller as a mutual mistake.
questions.explanation: D3 distinguishes an existing mistaken assumption from an unwanted future development. Other doctrines may address later events, but the formation-mistake analysis requires the relevant existing error.

questions.stem: A buyer knowingly accepts “unknown salvage contents, including the risk no usable pump remains.” What response must a mistake claim confront?
choices: The risk clause is irrelevant because the buyer did not know the exact contents of the crate.
The agreement may allocate the very uncertainty that occurred to the buyer.
A shared mistaken hope necessarily overrides any conscious allocation of the relevant uncertainty.
An expressly assumed risk disappears whenever the uncertain outcome substantially reduces value.
questions.explanation: The buyer’s acknowledged limited knowledge and express risk assumption are central. A mistake claim cannot ignore the bargain’s allocation of the asserted risk.

questions.stem: Which approach best fits the course unconscionability screen?
choices: Treat a standard form alone as sufficient, without examining meaningful choice or its terms.
Treat a high price alone as sufficient, without examining the bargaining process or applicable balance.
Examine bargaining-process defects and excessively one-sided terms under the applicable balance.
Evaluate unfairness only from later disappointment, without considering the agreement at formation.
questions.explanation: D3 calls for examining process and substance at formation, while recognizing variation in required balance and remedies. Neither standard form nor price alone decides the issue.

questions.stem: Match each described concern to the most directly relevant doctrine.
left: A material false inspection statement induces justified reliance
An improper threat induces assent with no reasonable alternative
Both parties share a basic existing error with material effect
Unfair persuasion exploits vulnerability in a dominant relationship
choices: Misrepresentation
Duress
Mutual mistake
Undue influence
questions.explanation: Each doctrine identifies a different defect. A complete analysis also checks its limits, including risk allocation for mistake and the facts supporting causation and reasonable alternatives.

questions.stem: An agreement that a protected party may elect to avoid is described as ___.
questions.explanation: Voidable differs from void and unenforceable. The relevant party’s ability to avoid, and any conditions on doing so, depend on the doctrine.

questions.stem: Which sequence best applies the course writing screen?
choices: Determine whether any oral promise was made, then treat that fact as a complete writing defense.
Identify the category, required content/signature, actual records and any limited exception.
Locate any signature, then presume every writing category and content requirement is satisfied.
Select an exception based on the claimed loss, without identifying its factual or quantity limits.
questions.explanation: D4–D6 separate a triggered writing requirement from satisfaction and exceptions. Formation and enforcement are distinct, and every exception has its own conditions.

questions.stem: A January 1 agreement requires continuous services from March 1 through the following February 28. Under D4, what matters for the one-year screen?
choices: Completion extends beyond a year from the January 1 making of the agreement.
The March 1 performance start controls, so the earlier date of making is irrelevant.
The expected service span alone controls, even if completion is later than a year after making.
A possible breach within a year constitutes full performance and removes the selected writing category.
questions.explanation: The clock starts at formation, not the service start date. The fixed performance end extends beyond a year from January 1; breach is not the promised full performance.

questions.stem: A report is expected to take fourteen months, but its terms allow full completion in eight. Under the selected D4 category, what is the best conclusion?
choices: The fourteen-month estimate triggers the rule even though full earlier completion is allowed.
The parties’ expected timetable becomes a mandatory minimum despite the terms permitting earlier completion.
Any task still unfinished after one year retroactively falls within the category regardless of its original terms.
Expected duration alone does not make full performance within a year impossible.
questions.explanation: D4 asks whether the agreement’s terms permit full performance within one year, not merely what duration seems likely. Other writing categories would need separate facts.

questions.stem: Under D5, a sufficient signed goods record shows ten units, while a claimant seeks one hundred. What does the record alone support through that writing rule?
choices: The writing permits enforcement of one hundred if the claimant later asserts that larger oral quantity.
The quantity mismatch makes the record unusable even for the ten units it sufficiently identifies.
Enforcement no further than its stated quantity of ten units.
The price threshold replaces quantity limits once a signed goods record indicates any sale.
questions.explanation: The goods writing rule tolerates some omissions but limits enforcement through the record to the quantity shown. Another route for additional units would need its own factual and legal basis.

questions.stem: Two merchants satisfy every D5 confirmation condition and no written objection is made within ten days. What follows from that route alone?
choices: It can satisfy the writing requirement against the recipient without proving the underlying bargain.
It conclusively proves the alleged oral agreement because failure to object operates as assent.
It removes the need to prove quantity because a confirmation supplies every disputed underlying term.
It establishes the recipient’s admission in court even though only silence after receipt is shown.
questions.explanation: The merchant-confirmation provision addresses the writing barrier. It does not eliminate a factual dispute about whether the parties actually made the alleged agreement.

questions.stem: An unwritten goods bargain concerns 30 mugs. The buyer receives and accepts six; no other exception facts are supplied. What is the scope of the D5 acceptance route?
choices: It supports the entire thirty-unit bargain because accepting part necessarily validates the whole quantity.
It supports none of the bargain because an exception cannot apply to fewer than all agreed goods.
It supports the writing exception for the six accepted mugs.
It supports the remaining twenty-four units first because those are the units still in dispute.
questions.explanation: Receipt and acceptance support the statutory path for the goods covered by that conduct. The remaining quantity needs another basis; the exception is not automatically all-or-nothing.

questions.stem: Which fact most directly supports D5’s specially manufactured goods route, assuming an otherwise valid contract?
choices: A substantial beginning after repudiation on buyer-specific goods otherwise unsuitable for ordinary resale.
A decision to customize goods before repudiation, without beginning manufacture or committing to procurement.
A substantial beginning before repudiation on goods suitable for ordinary resale to other buyers.
A substantial manufacturing beginning before repudiation on buyer-specific goods unsuitable for ordinary resale.
questions.explanation: The exception requires the special-resale characteristic and timely substantial beginning or procurement commitment in the specified circumstances. Intent to customize alone is insufficient.

questions.stem: A typed name appears in an email. What is the best D6 approach?
choices: Treat the displayed name alone as conclusive attribution and intent to adopt the email.
Check attribution, adoption as a signature, content and applicable electronic-record requirements.
Reject the email solely because the signature is electronic rather than handwritten.
Treat electronic form as sufficient even when the record omits required quantity or assent.
questions.explanation: Electronic form is not a universal defect or cure. D6 requires the relevant signature and record conditions; other substantive requirements remain.

questions.stem: Match each fact to its writing-screen role.
left: A goods record names 40 units
The defendant deliberately adopts a signature on the record
A qualifying confirmation draws a written objection within ten days
A party admits a specific quantity during testimony
choices: Quantity limit
Signature of party to be charged
Obstacle to the no-objection confirmation route
Potential in-court admission exception
questions.explanation: Each fact addresses a different requirement or exception. A timely objection defeats that confirmation route, not necessarily every other proof of an enforceable bargain.

questions.stem: The family of rules requiring a signed record for selected contract categories is commonly called the ___.
questions.explanation: The statute of frauds screens enforceability for specified categories. It does not mean every contract must be written or that actual fraud must be proved.

questions.stem: A term permits two plausible readings in context. What is the strongest initial interpretive method?
choices: Use the disputed word’s isolated dictionary meaning without reading the rest of the agreement.
Choose the meaning held privately by the drafter, without asking what was communicated.
Adopt the reading that produces the fairest result before checking textual and contextual support.
State both readings, then compare text, the whole agreement and permitted context.
questions.explanation: I1 requires a supported comparison. Whole-document context and communicated meaning matter; chronology of assertions and undisclosed wishes do not automatically control.

questions.stem: An agreement requires “delivery to Harbor by June 14,” states Harbor’s address and a June 15 event. What most strongly supports arrival by June 14?
choices: The seller’s later private shipping preference, without evidence that Harbor accepted it.
A dispatch-only meaning inferred solely from the fact that a carrier will transport the goods.
The destination language read with the address and event purpose.
The earlier general dispatch comment treated as controlling despite the final destination language.
questions.explanation: The particular text and purpose connect the deadline to arrival at the specified destination. Classification as goods does not by itself settle the delivery meaning.

questions.stem: Two parties disagree about a phrase. Why is disagreement alone insufficient to establish ambiguity?
choices: Any sincere disagreement establishes ambiguity even when one reading has no contextual support.
The proposed competing meanings must be reasonable in the relevant context.
Ambiguity requires proof that neither party understood any part of the bargain.
A signed agreement cannot contain ambiguity, regardless of the reasonable meanings of its terms.
questions.explanation: I1 distinguishes genuine plausible alternatives from a strained assertion. Disagreement signals an issue to investigate rather than proving ambiguity or universal invalidity.

questions.stem: Both parties attach materially different reasonable meanings to a key term and neither has reason to know the other’s meaning. Under I1, what issue arises?
choices: There may be no agreement on that term under the selected misunderstanding rule.
The drafter’s meaning controls solely because the drafter supplied the disputed words.
The later asserted meaning controls solely because it is the last explanation in the record.
A signature necessarily establishes a shared meaning despite the stipulated material misunderstanding.
questions.explanation: The selected rule considers material divergence and knowledge. The absence of reason to know can prevent agreement on the term; different knowledge facts can change the result.

questions.stem: A complete integration fixes a 3,000-dollar fee. An earlier email states 2,500 dollars and is offered only to replace that final price. Under I2, what is the problem?
choices: The earlier email controls because a written negotiation cannot be subject to the parol evidence screen.
The earlier price is a consistent addition merely because it appears in a separate document.
The earlier term contradicts the final integrated price.
The final writing excludes only spoken contradictions, leaving every prior written price enforceable.
questions.explanation: The parol evidence screen includes prior written agreements offered for this purpose. The contradiction, timing and finality matter; the rule is not limited to oral statements.

questions.stem: A signed agreement is complete on April 5. An April 8 exchange proposes an added workshop for an added fee. What is the proper first distinction?
choices: A complete integration permanently prevents the parties from making any later modification.
The later exchange raises modification issues, not merely exclusion of an earlier term.
The later exchange is enforceable solely because it occurs after the integrated writing.
The later exchange is treated as a prior negotiation whenever it concerns the same project.
questions.explanation: I2 distinguishes subsequent modification from prior or contemporaneous inconsistent terms. The change still requires its own assent, consideration or applicable alternative, and formalities.

questions.stem: Three earlier transactions between the same parties used cartons of 25. What contextual category best describes those transactions?
choices: Course of dealing.
Course of performance under the current agreement.
Usage of trade established solely by this pair’s prior transactions.
A later modification of the current packing term.
questions.explanation: I3 uses course of dealing for previous transactions between the parties. Conduct under the current agreement is performance; a broader established practice is trade usage.

questions.stem: Under I3’s selected hierarchy, an express packing term and a qualifying trade usage cannot reasonably be reconciled; no waiver is established. Which generally has priority?
choices: The trade usage, solely because an established industry practice overrides express language.
The usage if it predates the contract, because earlier practices take priority over later express terms.
Neither, because any irreconcilable usage automatically destroys the entire agreement.
The express term.
questions.explanation: The selected hierarchy prioritizes express terms when reasonable reconciliation fails. Classification, notice and waiver still matter, but no waiver is supplied here.

questions.stem: Match each item to the appropriate interpretation concept.
left: Writing adopted as final for stated terms but not exhaustive
Writing adopted as the exclusive complete statement within its scope
Repeated knowing conduct under this agreement
Established practice in the relevant trade
choices: Partial integration
Complete integration
Course of performance
Usage of trade
questions.explanation: Finality and completeness are different. Performance concerns this transaction; trade usage concerns an established practice beyond the parties’ private preference.

questions.stem: The rule screening certain earlier or contemporaneous agreements offered to contradict or supplement a final writing is the ___ rule.
questions.explanation: The parol evidence rule is not limited to spoken statements and must be distinguished from interpretation, validity challenges and later modifications.

questions.stem: Under G1, the parties leave a nonessential goods term open. Which answer correctly identifies what supports formation without requiring every term to be settled?
choices: Intent to contract and a reasonably certain basis for a remedy.
A court’s ability to select any missing quantity without identifying an actual quantity commitment.
Every term must appear in matching forms, including details the parties intentionally left open.
A precise formation instant must be established even if agreement and a remedial basis otherwise exist.
questions.explanation: Article 2 permits flexibility where agreement and a sufficient remedial basis exist. It does not authorize unlimited invention of missing essential commitments.

questions.stem: A prompt order calls for blue folders. The seller promptly ships green folders with no accommodation notice. Under G3, what can this shipment do?
choices: Prevent formation because any shipment varying from the order must be a counteroffer.
Accept the offer while also breaching the color requirement.
Accept the offer and silently replace the color term merely by shipping a different color.
Operate as an accommodation solely because the seller lacks conforming folders, without seasonable notice.
questions.explanation: G3 separates acceptance from conformity. Nonconforming shipment can accept and breach; the stipulated accommodation notice that would change its role is absent.

questions.stem: Before sending substitute folders, the seller seasonably says they are offered only as an accommodation. What follows under G3?
choices: The notice obligates the buyer to accept the substitute shipment as performance of the original order.
The shipment accepts the original offer despite the stipulated seasonable accommodation notice.
The notice modifies the original color requirement without any assent from the buyer.
That shipment does not constitute acceptance of the original order under this rule.
questions.explanation: The accommodation qualification prevents this shipment from operating as acceptance under G3. Any later agreement depends on additional facts, including the buyer’s response.

questions.stem: A merchant’s qualifying signed goods assurance says an offer stays open six months, with no option consideration. Under G2, how long can statutory firm-offer irrevocability last?
choices: Six months automatically, because any stated assurance overrides the statutory cap.
A reasonable period potentially exceeding three months under this provision alone.
No more than three months under this provision.
No protected period, because a merchant’s signed assurance still requires option consideration.
questions.explanation: G2’s statutory protection has a three-month cap. A supported option could supply a separate longer protection, and expiration of protection does not itself necessarily terminate the offer.

questions.stem: A definite timely goods acceptance adds a clause but is not expressly conditional. Under G4, what should be analyzed separately?
choices: Whether the last form supersedes earlier terms solely because it was sent last.
Whether a contract formed and whether the added term enters it.
Whether every additional clause necessarily prevents acceptance under the sales framework.
Whether merchant status alone incorporates every new clause without applying any exception.
questions.explanation: G4 can recognize formation despite additional terms. Inclusion depends on the additional-terms rules and exceptions, rather than a universal last-form or merchant-silence rule.

questions.stem: In Harbor R7–R8, what is the best conclusion about arbitration under the stipulated facts?
choices: The extra clause defeats formation because the common-law mirror-image rule controls this goods acceptance.
The clause enters solely because both parties are merchants despite the stated limitation and materiality.
The clause enters unless Harbor countersigns an express rejection, regardless of material alteration.
The contract forms, but the addition does not enter automatically given the offer limitation and material alteration.
questions.explanation: R8 is definite, timely and nonconditional, supporting formation. R7’s limitation and the stipulated material nature of arbitration block automatic incorporation; Harbor never expressly assents.

questions.stem: Writings fail to form a goods contract because acceptance is expressly conditional and the condition is not accepted. Both parties then ship and pay in recognition of a contract. Under G4’s conduct route, where do terms come from?
choices: All terms of the conditional seller form, because shipping and payment necessarily accept every clause.
Only terms from the first form, because later conduct makes the original offer control every gap.
Agreed written terms plus applicable statutory supplements.
No terms at all, because failure of the writings prevents a contract through conduct.
questions.explanation: Subsection (3)’s selected conduct route uses agreement and statutory supplements. Performance is not automatic assent to every contested conditional-form term.

questions.stem: In the actual Harbor record, the board approves and R5 includes the room cost in the signed price. Which statement best handles the deposit?
choices: Address the untriggered decline condition and inclusive price before seeking any separate reimbursement.
The original deposit must be reimbursed separately solely because it was incurred before R5.
The entire tablet and deposit cost must be added because both supported the consultant’s general work.
The board’s approval itself triggers the decline contingency, making the later room-cost term immaterial.
questions.explanation: R4 is approval, not the separate decline variation. R5 includes the room cost; the model therefore rejects automatic duplicate payment. The earlier tablet was not induced by the reimbursement promise.

questions.stem: Match the Harbor issue to the most directly relevant rule set.
left: Lumen’s unchanged-work bonus in R6
Paperline’s nonconditional response with arbitration in R8
Signed 200-notebook order in R7
Arrival versus dispatch under R7–R9
choices: Common-law existing-duty modification rule
Sales formation and additional-terms rules
Goods writing and quantity requirements
Interpretation and final-expression rules
questions.explanation: The capstone needs multiple distinct analyses. Using one rule for every issue would conflate consideration, formation, enforceability and meaning.

questions.stem: A seasonably identified substitute shipment offered only for the buyer’s consideration is an ___ under G3.
questions.explanation: An accommodation notice changes the shipment’s role under the selected prompt-shipment acceptance rule. It does not force acceptance of the substitutes.

decks.title: Contracts I: Formation and Interpretation notecards

cards.front: What should you classify before applying acceptance rules?
cards.back: The transaction: goods, services, land or a mixed exchange under the supplied governing test.

cards.front: Does Article 2 apply only when both parties are merchants?
cards.back: No. It governs covered sales of goods; particular rules have additional merchant conditions.

cards.front: Which facts inform the course predominant-purpose test?
cards.back: The buyer’s main objective, contract language, supplier’s business and price allocation; no single label automatically decides.

cards.front: What does objective assent exclude as controlling by itself?
cards.back: An undisclosed private intention. Communicated reservations and known context still matter.

cards.front: What power does an offer give its recipient?
cards.back: The invited assent can conclude a sufficiently definite proposed bargain without another reserved decision.

cards.front: Why may a starting-price quote be preliminary?
cards.back: It may leave scope or approval unresolved and invite a further proposal rather than present acceptance.

cards.front: Can an advertisement ever function as an offer?
cards.back: Yes, if specificity and context communicate the required commitment; “advertisement” is not a conclusive label.

cards.front: What must an analysis do with an express signature reservation?
cards.back: Address whether the required signature occurred or the reservation was otherwise removed under supplied facts and rules.

cards.front: How do a conditional acceptance and a separate request differ?
cards.back: A conditional response makes assent depend on a new bargain; an unconditional acceptance can stand alongside a request.

cards.front: Can an unsolicited offer ordinarily make silence acceptance?
cards.back: No. A stated silence clause alone does not establish assent; exception facts require separate analysis.

cards.front: What does an express receipt deadline do to the postal default?
cards.back: It controls. Posting before the deadline does not satisfy a required receipt after the deadline.

cards.front: Is asking about a lower price necessarily rejection?
cards.back: No. A mere inquiry can differ from a counteroffer; read whether the response actually conditions assent or rejects the offer.

cards.front: When does ordinary revocation usually take effect under F2?
cards.back: On receipt, subject to the course’s rule for reliable information and other qualifications.

cards.front: When does the limited F3 postal acceptance rule apply?
cards.back: To properly dispatched invited postal acceptance of an ordinary offer without a controlling receipt requirement.

cards.front: What is the course timing rule for option acceptance?
cards.back: Receipt, not the ordinary dispatch default, unless a supplied governing term changes the analysis.

cards.front: What does beginning invited unilateral performance protect?
cards.back: An opportunity to complete within the allowed or reasonable time; starting alone does not earn payment conditioned on completion.

cards.front: What are the two sides of a consideration explanation?
cards.back: The promise and the return promise or performance sought and given in exchange.

cards.front: Why can giving up a legal freedom be consideration?
cards.back: The surrender can be the bargained-for return even without physical harm or a financial loss.

cards.front: Does a genuine low-price sale necessarily lack consideration?
cards.back: No. Economic adequacy and the existence of an actual bargain are separate.

cards.front: How does a gift condition differ from bargained work?
cards.back: A gift condition may facilitate receipt; bargained work is requested as the price of the promise.

cards.front: Why is an unbargained past act ordinarily insufficient?
cards.back: It was completed before, and not sought in exchange for, the later promise.

cards.front: What makes a promise illusory?
cards.back: Complete retained discretion can leave no meaningful undertaking; genuine good-faith requirements can impose a real constraint.

cards.front: What is the basic common-law modification concern with unchanged work?
cards.back: Doing only an existing duty to the same promisor ordinarily provides no fresh consideration for extra pay.

cards.front: What remains important for a goods modification without new consideration?
cards.back: Assent, good faith and applicable writing or signed-modification requirements.

cards.front: What must a reliance analysis identify before discussing expenses?
cards.back: The specific promise, including its scope, conditions and any cap.

cards.front: Why does an expense predating the promise fail a causal reliance argument?
cards.back: The later promise could not have induced an already completed purchase.

cards.front: What does foreseeable reliance ask?
cards.back: Whether the promisor should reasonably anticipate the action or forbearance claimed.

cards.front: What can weaken the reasonableness of reliance?
cards.back: Known approval conditions, express limits or spending beyond the undertaking reasonably communicated.

cards.front: Why does a refund matter under F7?
cards.back: It changes remaining detriment and the need or extent of enforcement to avoid injustice.

cards.front: Can consideration and reliance be argued in the alternative?
cards.back: Yes, if each theory is analyzed; alternate grounds do not authorize duplicate recovery for the same loss.

cards.front: Does promissory estoppel always override a writing requirement?
cards.back: No. The relevant exception or interaction requires a supplied rule or jurisdictional research.

cards.front: How does restitution’s focus differ?
cards.back: It concerns unjustly retained benefits, rather than automatically enforcing a promise or reimbursing every expense.

cards.front: How does voidable differ from void?
cards.back: Voidable describes a protected party’s power to avoid; void indicates no legal effect in the relevant sense. Specific consequences require the doctrine.

cards.front: Does a diagnosis alone decide contractual capacity?
cards.back: No. Apply the governing capacity test to the transaction and relevant functional facts.

cards.front: What links misrepresentation to avoidance under D2?
cards.back: A fraudulent or material false assertion must induce assent through justified reliance.

cards.front: What is missing from financial pressure alone as duress?
cards.back: An improper threat causing assent without a reasonable alternative.

cards.front: What does mutual mistake require beyond shared error?
cards.back: A basic assumption, material effect and a claimant who does not bear the relevant risk.

cards.front: Why is a later price decline different from an existing destroyed item?
cards.back: A future development differs from an erroneous fact already present at formation.

cards.front: What must a risk-allocation analysis inspect?
cards.back: Express terms, conscious acceptance of limited knowledge and other applicable assignments of uncertainty.

cards.front: Why is a high price alone insufficient for the course unconscionability screen?
cards.back: The selected framework also examines bargaining process and substantive one-sidedness, with jurisdictional variation.

cards.front: What are the four steps in the writing screen?
cards.back: Category, required content and signature, actual records, then any exception with its limits.

cards.front: When does the one-year clock start under D4?
cards.back: When the agreement is made, not when performance begins.

cards.front: Does an expected fourteen-month project necessarily trigger the selected one-year category?
cards.back: No, if full performance within one year is possible under its terms; expectation alone is insufficient.

cards.front: Whose signature is important in the basic writing requirement?
cards.back: The party against whom enforcement is sought, subject to agents and specified exceptions.

cards.front: What quantity can a signed goods record support through that writing alone?
cards.back: No more than the quantity shown; additional enforcement needs another supported basis.

cards.front: What does merchant confirmation not prove by itself?
cards.back: That the alleged underlying agreement actually existed or included every disputed fact.

cards.front: What limits the receipt-and-acceptance goods exception?
cards.back: It covers the goods received and accepted, not automatically every alleged unit.

cards.front: Why is electronic form not a universal cure or defect?
cards.back: Relevant signature and record requirements must be met, and substantive assent, capacity and content requirements remain.

cards.front: What makes an interpretation paragraph useful?
cards.back: It states competing plausible readings and connects each to the whole text and permitted context.

cards.front: Does disagreement by itself prove ambiguity?
cards.back: No. The competing readings must be reasonable in the relevant context.

cards.front: What supports arrival in “delivery to Harbor by June 14”?
cards.back: The destination wording, stated address and next-day distribution purpose, read with the record’s limits.

cards.front: What knowledge matters in a misunderstanding problem?
cards.back: Whether either party knows or has reason to know the other’s materially different meaning.

cards.front: How does partial integration differ from complete integration?
cards.back: Both can be final; only complete integration is also the exclusive full statement within its scope.

cards.front: Is the parol evidence rule limited to oral statements?
cards.back: No. Earlier written terms can also be screened when offered to contradict or supplement a final writing.

cards.front: Why analyze a later modification separately?
cards.back: It arises after the final writing and needs its own formation and enforceability analysis rather than automatic exclusion as an earlier term.

cards.front: How do performance, dealing and usage differ?
cards.back: Performance concerns this agreement; dealing concerns prior transactions between these parties; usage concerns an established trade practice.

cards.front: When can open goods terms coexist with formation?
cards.back: When intent to contract and a sufficiently certain basis for a remedy remain under the supplied rule; this does not authorize inventing any quantity.

cards.front: Can a nonconforming shipment both accept and breach?
cards.back: Yes under the selected prompt-shipment rule, unless the seasonable accommodation qualification applies.

cards.front: What does an accommodation notice do?
cards.back: It identifies the substitute shipment as an alternative, preventing that shipment from accepting under the selected rule.

cards.front: What caps statutory firm-offer protection under G2?
cards.back: Three months without consideration under that provision; an independently supported option may protect longer.

cards.front: What two questions must be separated under the forms rule?
cards.back: Whether an acceptance formed a contract and whether an additional term enters the contract.

cards.front: Why does Harbor not automatically accept the arbitration addition?
cards.back: Its order limits acceptance and the addition is stipulated material; Harbor never expressly assents.

cards.front: What terms govern the conduct-only formation path in G4?
cards.back: Agreed written terms plus applicable statutory supplements, not every term in the last conditional form.

cards.front: Why does the actual Harbor deposit analysis differ from the decline variation?
cards.back: The board actually approves and R5 includes the room cost; the express decline condition is not triggered and duplicate reimbursement is not automatic.

An apparent promise that reserves complete discretion and imposes no meaningful obligation on its maker.
An obligation already owed; merely performing it for the same promisor ordinarily does not supply new consideration for a common-law modification.
An agreed change to an existing contract, subject to the applicable assent, consideration or alternative, good-faith and formality rules.

A communicated commitment to act or refrain from acting in a specified way, distinguished from mere interest or prediction.
A change of position made because of a promise or representation; the particular doctrine also determines required reasonableness and detriment.
The connection showing that the asserted promise or statement actually induced the claimed action or forbearance.
A change of position justified in the circumstances, including the promise’s scope, conditions and known uncertainties.
Refraining from an action, such as declining an available opportunity, which may be relevant to exchange or reliance.

A final writing that is not a complete and exclusive statement of the agreement within the relevant scope.
A writing adopted as the complete and exclusive statement of the agreement within its scope.
The rule governing certain prior or contemporaneous agreements offered to contradict or supplement a final writing; not limited to oral evidence.
Language stating a writing’s intended finality or completeness, whose effect requires the governing rules and context.
Qualifying repeated conduct under the particular agreement, with knowledge and opportunity for objection or acquiescence.
A relevant pattern from earlier transactions between the same parties.
A sufficiently established practice in the relevant trade that can inform agreement under applicable qualification and notice rules.

A shipment departing from the order that can operate as acceptance and breach under the course prompt-shipment rule unless the accommodation qualification applies.
A seasonably identified substitute shipment offered only as an alternative for the buyer’s consideration, rather than acceptance under the selected shipment rule.
The formation and term-inclusion problem arising when exchanged commercial documents contain nonmatching terms.

references.title: Exercise rules: defenses and writing requirements
references.body:
## Stipulated teaching rules

These original D rules govern the fictional exercises only. They organize introductory issues without covering every exception, remedy or jurisdiction. Formation, enforceability and the extent of relief are separate questions.

### D1 — Capacity and avoidance

An ordinary minor's contract is generally voidable at the minor's election under the course rule, not automatically nonexistent or void for both parties. Necessaries, ratification after majority, restitution duties and statutory exceptions need separate rules. For mental incapacity, investigate ability to understand the transaction or act reasonably in relation to it and the other party's knowledge under the applicable test; a diagnosis alone is not the answer. The course does not supply a universal mental-capacity test. “Voidable” means a protected party may avoid an otherwise operative agreement; “unenforceable” describes a barrier to enforcement; “void” indicates no legal effect. Use the particular doctrine rather than treating these labels as synonyms.

### D2 — Misrepresentation, duress and undue influence

For exercise avoidance based on misrepresentation, require a fraudulent or material false assertion, inducement of assent and justified reliance. A fact can be material without deliberate lying. An opinion, silence or nondisclosure needs further circumstances before being treated as a qualifying assertion; do not assume every silence is fraud. For duress require an improper threat that induces assent while leaving no reasonable alternative. Financial difficulty alone does not establish duress. Undue influence concerns unfair persuasion within a relationship of vulnerability or domination; friendship alone is insufficient. Timely avoidance, restoration and affirmation are additional real-law issues beyond these introductory questions.

### D3 — Mistake and unfairness

For mutual mistake, both parties must share an erroneous belief at formation about a basic assumption, with a material effect on the exchange, and the party seeking avoidance must not bear the risk. Express risk allocation and conscious acceptance of limited knowledge matter. A later change or disappointing forecast is not the same as an erroneous existing fact. Unilateral mistake needs additional grounds under the applicable law; a one-party arithmetic error is not automatically a release. For course unconscionability problems, examine both defects in bargaining process and excessively one-sided terms at formation. The required balance and remedies vary. A high price alone is not conclusive. Illegal purpose or public policy can also block enforcement; identify the actual prohibition or policy before declaring an agreement void.

### D4 — Common-law writing screen

For these exercises a signed memorandum identifying the bargain and its essential terms is generally required to enforce a land transfer or an agreement that, by its terms at formation, cannot be fully performed within one year of making. Signatures are assessed against the party to be charged. The one-year clock starts when the agreement is made, not when performance starts. Long expected duration is insufficient if completion within a year is possible under its terms. Potential breach or a cancellation right is not automatically full performance. These are selected categories; guarantees, marriage-related promises and specialized statutes require further research. Exceptions for full performance, part performance and estoppel are not assumed unless the problem supplies them.

### D5 — Goods writing screen

Use a 500-dollar-or-more price threshold in the course goods problems, following the cited Article 2 text. Seek a signed writing indicating a sales contract and specifying a quantity; enforcement through that writing cannot exceed the quantity shown. Under the between-merchants confirmation rule, a timely confirmation sufficient against its sender can satisfy the writing requirement against its recipient if received with reason to know its contents and not objected to in writing within ten days. This does not itself prove an underlying agreement.

Three statutory paths can matter without a sufficient writing: specially manufactured goods unsuitable for ordinary resale, after a substantial beginning or procurement commitment before repudiation; an in-court admission, limited to admitted quantity; and payment made and accepted or goods received and accepted, limited to the covered goods. Each requires the relevant facts and an otherwise valid contract. A private out-of-court statement is not automatically the in-court admission exception. Partial payment is not a universal license to enforce every claimed unit.

### D6 — Electronic form

For exercises stating that electronic-record requirements are met, a deliberately adopted typed signature can satisfy the signature requirement. Establish attribution, intent, accessible content and applicable law. Electronic form does not cure missing assent, quantity or capacity. Do not assume a displayed name is always a signature, or that federal electronic-signature law compels everyone to accept electronic dealings.

## Primary-law reading

[Enacted Washington Article 2, including 62A.2-201 and 62A.2-302](https://app.leg.wa.gov/rcw/default.aspx?cite=62A.2&full=true) is an illustrative state enactment, not the chosen jurisdiction for this course. Compare its use of “record” with the [UCC 2-201 text reproduced by Cornell](https://www.law.cornell.edu/ucc/2/2-201). [15 U.S.C. 7001](https://uscode.house.gov/us/usc/119-124/t15/s7001/) addresses electronic form while preserving other requirements and qualifications. [Martinez-Gonzalez v. Elkhorn Packing Co., amended Ninth Circuit opinion, February 14, 2022](https://cdn.ca9.uscourts.gov/datastore/opinions/2022/02/14/19-17311.pdf) illustrates application of California duress law; it is not a nationwide contract code.

Further jurisdiction-specific examples: [Dodson v. Shrader, 824 S.W.2d 545, 547–49 (Tenn. 1992)](https://law.justia.com/cases/tennessee/supreme-court/1992/824-s-w-2d-545-2.html) illustrates minors' avoidance and state-specific restoration limits; [Lenawee County Board of Health v. Messerly, 417 Mich. 17, 24–33 (1982)](https://law.justia.com/cases/michigan/supreme-court/1982/65513-3.html) addresses existing mutual mistake and allocated risk. [Wilson v. 2 Tower, LLC, No. WC-2017-0018, pp. 12–15 (R.I. Super. Ct. Sept. 20, 2022)](https://www.courts.ri.gov/Decisions/17-0018.pdf) is a trial-court illustration of material misrepresentation, justified reliance and a merger clause; it is not a nationwide rule. For the writing screen compare New York General Obligations Law [5-701(a)(1)](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/GOB/5-701) and [5-703(2)](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/GOB/5-703). These examples do not select a governing state for the course.

references.title: Exercise rules: assent, exchange and reliance
references.body:
## How to use these rules

The numbered rules below are original, simplified teaching assumptions for this course's fictional problems. They are not a statute, judicial opinion, Restatement quotation or statement of identical law across the United States. Use them when an exercise says “course rules.” Real analysis requires the governing jurisdiction, current enacted text and relevant precedent. Sources and differences are identified in the companion references. Do not cite “F1” as real authority outside this course.

### F1 — Governing framework and objective assent

Use common-law teaching rules for services and land; use the course Article 2 rules for sales of movable goods. For a mixed transaction, use its predominant purpose as the exercise's chosen test, considering the language, supplier's business, value allocation and buyer's objective. Other courts may use different approaches. Assess assent through words and conduct as a reasonable recipient would understand them in context. Secret intent alone does not defeat apparent assent. A known joke, an understood reservation of approval or materially different reasonable meanings can change the result.

### F2 — Offer and power of acceptance

An offer communicates a present willingness to contract on sufficiently definite terms so the invited assent would conclude the bargain. Advertisements, price quotes and preliminary negotiations usually invite offers, but specificity and commitment can change their significance. An offer ends by effective revocation, rejection, counteroffer, lapse or a party's death/incapacity, subject to applicable exceptions. In ordinary revocable offers, revocation is effective on receipt; reliable information of inconsistent action can also terminate the power to accept. An inquiry does not necessarily reject an offer. A deadline alone does not purchase irrevocability.

### F3 — Acceptance and timing

For common-law exercises, acceptance must express assent to the proposed bargain; a conditional change is a counteroffer, while an unequivocal acceptance plus a request can be effective. Follow an unambiguous required method or receipt condition. Otherwise a reasonable invited method may suffice. Silence ordinarily is not acceptance; a known and accepted benefit or an established course of dealing may supply facts for an exception. For properly dispatched, invited postal acceptance of an ordinary offer, the course uses dispatch as the effective moment. Revocation must be received first to defeat that acceptance. An option acceptance is effective on receipt; an explicit receipt requirement controls. Do not extend this postal rule automatically to email, texts or an acceptance sent after a rejection; those issues require additional rules.

### F4 — Keeping an offer open

A supported option exchanges consideration for a promise to hold an offer open. During its protected period, an attempted revocation does not terminate the power to accept; rejection or counteroffer ordinarily does not terminate it either under the course option rule. If an offer invites only completed performance, beginning the actual invited performance creates temporary protection against revocation, conditioned on completion within the allowed or reasonable time. Mere preparation is not the same as beginning performance, though reliance may merit separate analysis. A merchant firm offer for goods follows G2 in the sales reference, not the ordinary option requirements.

### F5 — Consideration

A promise or performance is consideration when sought and given in exchange for the other promise. Giving up a legal freedom can count. Courts ordinarily do not compare economic adequacy, but a sham recital without an actual bargain is different from a genuine low-price exchange. A completed past act ordinarily cannot supply the later bargain; gratitude and moral obligation alone do not establish it. A gift condition may merely arrange delivery rather than purchase a return performance. A wholly discretionary promise may be illusory. A genuine good-faith requirements obligation can constrain discretion. In goods transactions, the cited Article 2 rule also restricts demands unreasonably disproportionate to a stated estimate or otherwise comparable prior requirements. Special material-benefit, charitable and statutory exceptions are outside these basic exercises unless supplied.

### F6 — Existing duties and changes

For these common-law problems, doing only what one already owes the same promisor ordinarily supplies no fresh consideration for a modification. A genuinely additional duty can supply it. A fair modification responding to unanticipated circumstances may be enforceable under a separately stated exception; the basic rule alone does not resolve every real jurisdiction. Article 2 modifications need no new consideration but require good faith and applicable formalities. A threat manufactured to extract a concession is not rescued by the no-new-consideration rule.

### F7 — Reliance

Use promissory estoppel as a distinct possible ground: identify a sufficiently definite promise, reasonably foreseeable action or forbearance, actual reasonable detrimental reliance caused by the promise, and a need for enforcement to avoid injustice. Analyze each link; loss alone does not prove a promise. Relief may be limited to what justice requires; it is not automatically the entire promised benefit. Do not assume reliance overrides a statute of frauds or other defense; that interaction requires a supplied rule or jurisdictional research. Restitution instead focuses on an unjustly retained benefit and is only a boundary concept here.

## Primary-law reading

These are jurisdiction-specific illustrations, not a national contract code or the source of every stipulated F rule.

- [Lucy v. Zehmer, 196 Va. 493, 503–04 (1954)](https://law.justia.com/cases/virginia/supreme-court/1954/4272-1.html): outward assent and context.
- [Lefkowitz v. Great Minneapolis Surplus Store, 251 Minn. 188, 191–92 (1957)](https://law.justia.com/cases/minnesota/supreme-court/1957/37-220.html): an unusually definite advertisement can be an offer.
- [Normile v. Miller, 326 S.E.2d 11, 15–18 (N.C. 1985)](https://law.justia.com/cases/north-carolina/supreme-court/1985/487pa83-0.html): counteroffers, option limits and notice of revocation. Do not assume a counteroffer carries forward every term of the first offer.
- [Santos v. Dean, 96 Wash. App. 849, 854–56 (1999)](https://www.casemine.com/judgement/us/5914baf4add7b04934793df2/amp): option acceptance and the receipt rule; the opinion acknowledges differing approaches.
- [Hamer v. Sidway, 124 N.Y. 538, 545–46 (1891)](https://www.nycourts.gov/reporter/archives/hamer_sidway.htm): bargained-for surrender of legal freedom.
- [Angel v. Murray, 322 A.2d 630, 634–38 (R.I. 1974)](https://law.justia.com/cases/rhode-island/supreme-court/1974/322-a-2d-630-0.html): existing duties and a fair, voluntary modification responding to unanticipated circumstances.
- [UCC 2-306](https://www.law.cornell.edu/ucc/2/2-306): requirements/output quantities and good faith. [UCC 2-209](https://www.law.cornell.edu/ucc/2/2-209) supplies the sales-modification comparison. These are model-text reproductions; enacted state law and controlling decisions govern real disputes.

For reliance, [Doron v. Eastern Washington University, No. 31636-0-III, pp. 52–56 (Wash. Ct. App. Dec. 9, 2014)](https://www.courts.wa.gov/opinions/pdf/316360.unp.pdf) discusses Washington promissory-estoppel elements and the need for an actual promise. This is an unpublished opinion, supplied as a reading example rather than binding authority. Research current governing precedent for an actual case.

references.title: Harbor Workshop: model analysis and self-assessment
references.body:
## Read after completing your draft

This is one supported analysis of the fictional record, not a real legal opinion. Use the stipulated teaching rules and record IDs. Other well-supported organization and phrasing are welcome. The model separates conclusions that the record resolves from issues requiring additional law or facts.

## Service formation: the later signed agreement controls

The Harbor–Lumen transaction purchases planning and rehearsal services, so F1 directs us to the common-law teaching framework. R1 expressly postpones the workshop contract until board approval and both signatures. The coordinator's favorable response does not satisfy those conditions. The April 5 approval in R4 resolves one condition but leaves signatures outstanding. A claim that the full workshop contract arose April 1 would disregard the parties' communicated reservation.

R5 supplies the later agreement. Both parties sign after approval and commit to a defined plan and rehearsal for 1,800 dollars, with room costs included. Lumen's services are sought for Harbor's payment promise, and vice versa, supplying consideration under F5. The earlier absence of a contract does not prevent formation on April 8. R5 also states the final and complete terms of that project. The record supplies no capacity or consent defense; the analysis should not invent one merely because defenses are part of the course.

## Deposit: distinguish actual facts from the alternative

R2 is narrower than the proposed workshop contract. It promises reimbursement if approval fails and requests a room reservation. R3 documents a 240-dollar nonrefundable payment caused by that message. If the board had declined, the promised reimbursement, foreseeable booking, actual loss, reasonable reliance within the cap and lack of a refund would strongly support a claim under F7. A bargain theory would also deserve analysis because Harbor expressly requested the reservation; it may be the return sought for the reimbursement undertaking. Missing final approval of the larger project does not automatically defeat this separate promise.

In the actual record, however, the board approves. The express decline condition is not triggered, and R5 includes the room cost within the 1,800-dollar price. Lumen should not receive a separate 240 dollars merely by counting the same cost under several theories. R5's integration and explicit room term further support treating the agreed price as covering the deposit. The 700-dollar tablet purchase predates all relevant promises and served general work, so it was not caused by R2. Nothing in R5 promises to reimburse it. Reliance analysis must track the particular promise and expense.

## Bonus: assent does not resolve consideration

R6 shows assent to a higher fee but no additional undertaking by Lumen. The same plan and rehearsal are already owed under R5. Under the stipulated F6 common-law rule, that existing duty supplies no new consideration for the bonus. There are no unanticipated circumstances, new duties, qualifying reliance or supplied exception to support the change. The electronic signature establishes the adopted message under D6 but does not itself cure the consideration problem. The strongest course conclusion is that the extra 100 dollars lacks support under the specified modification rule; this does not invalidate the original R5 bargain.

## Notebook formation and the arbitration addition

The Paperline transaction purchases 200 movable notebooks with incidental printing, making Article 2 the course framework. R7 supplies a specific offer. R8 is a definite, timely, nonconditional acceptance, so G4 supports formation even though the response adds arbitration. Applying a strict common-law mirror-image rule would skip the selected sales rule.

The term question follows formation. Both parties are merchants, but R7 limits acceptance to its terms, R8's arbitration addition is stipulated to be material, and Harbor never expressly agrees to it. These facts block automatic incorporation through the between-merchants additional-terms rule. The supported conclusion is a notebook contract without treating the added arbitration clause as part of it on this record. This analysis does not establish that every arbitration provision is always material. Nor is it necessary to invoke the conduct-only formation route: the writings already form the contract, and R10 supplies no subsequent conduct supporting a different path.

## Writing requirements and defenses

The service agreement can be fully performed within one year of April 8 and does not transfer land, so D4's selected common-law categories do not create a writing barrier. R5 is signed in any event. Do not infer that its signature alone decides every possible statutory issue; the exercise supplies no other category. The notebook price exceeds D5's selected threshold, and R7 identifies the bargain and quantity and bears Harbor's adopted signature. The exercise stipulates the relevant electronic requirements. R7 therefore satisfies the stated writing screen for enforcement against Harbor up to its stated 200 notebooks. Paperline's R8 also confirms the matched bargain, but no merchant-confirmation silence theory is needed to establish Harbor's signed record.

R10 supplies no receipt-and-acceptance, admission or manufacturing exception facts. Inventing them would make the answer less accurate, not more thorough. No supplied fact supports mistake, misrepresentation, duress, incapacity or illegality. A real client interview would check those matters; this closed-record exercise has resolved them.

## Delivery: arrival is the stronger reading

R7 and R8 both require delivery to Harbor by June 14. The destination address and June 15 distribution purpose support arrival at the workshop, not merely dispatch to a carrier. Paperline's strongest stated response is its April 9 comment about usually sending orders the day before an event. But Harbor did not agree to that allocation, and the later matching delivery term is stipulated to be final. Under I1 and I2, a prior general practice statement is weak support for contradicting the specific destination commitment. R9 also rules out an established dealing, trade usage or performance practice that might support an alternative contextual argument.

Arrival is therefore the better interpretation on the supplied record. Paperline's proposed June 14 dispatch for June 16 arrival would not satisfy that meaning, but no shipment has occurred. The memo should distinguish interpreting the obligation from deciding completed breach, anticipatory-repudiation doctrine, damages or assurance procedures. Those require the next course's rules. This conclusion identifies the contractual commitment while keeping remedy claims within the record's limits.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score each dimension 0–2: 0 missing or materially wrong; 1 partly supported with an important omission; 2 accurate, fact-linked and appropriately qualified. Total 16 is a revision aid, not an accredited assessment or automatic app grade.

| Dimension | What a strong response does |
|---|---|
| Framework | Separates services and goods and explains the classification |
| Formation | Preserves approval/signature conditions and locates later service formation |
| Exchange | Identifies R5's consideration and R6's existing-duty problem |
| Reliance | Tests promise, causation and reasonable loss; separates actual facts and variation |
| Sales terms | Separates R8 formation from the arbitration addition and its stipulated limits |
| Enforceability | Applies category, signature and quantity screens without invented exceptions |
| Meaning | Compares arrival and dispatch using final language and permitted context |
| Method | Uses record/rule IDs, counterarguments and precise limits without double recovery |

## Revision workshop

Weak: “Harbor liked the proposal, so everything was binding immediately.”

Better: “R1 expressly reserves approval and signatures. R4 supplies approval but not signatures; R5 supplies both parties' signatures and the reciprocal service promises.”

Weak: “The seller's form came last, so arbitration governs.”

Better: “R8 can accept under G4 without incorporating arbitration. R7 limits acceptance, and the addition is stipulated to be material; Harbor never assents to it.”

Weak: “Lumen spent 940 dollars, so Harbor owes all of it.”

Better: “The 700-dollar tablet predates the promise. The 240-dollar deposit was induced by R2, but the actual approval and R5's inclusive price must be addressed before claiming a separate payment.”

## Further variations

Change only one fact at a time: remove R1's signature reservation; make R8 expressly conditional; add a signed goods quantity of only 100; or substitute “shipment” for “delivery to Harbor.” For each variation, state which rule changes the analysis and which conclusions remain supported. Do not use the original model's conclusion without checking the changed fact.
